extracted.intended_audience: researchers, data stewards, policy makers and practitioners in life sciences (especially human genomics) involved in research data management and data sharing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for making research data Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR), plus cross-cutting requirements for metadata, machine-actionability, access control, governance, ethics, and incentives—with a focus on human genomics but applicable across life sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findability
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets should be described, identified and registered or indexed in a clear and unequivocal manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign a unique and persistent identifier to datasets; systematically specify main characteristics, ideally using standard formats; store or index metadata in a public resource (example: BBMRI-ERIC Directory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets should be accessible through a clearly defined access procedure, ideally using automated means. Metadata should always remain accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish authentication and authorisation procedures and implement automated data retrieval protocols where appropriate; ensure metadata remains accessible even if underlying data are unavailable (example: European genome–phenome archive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperability
rubrics_metrics.description: Data and metadata are conceptualised, expressed and structured using common, published standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw on standard technical and semantic data formats, variables, ontologies and the like; ensure such standards are themselves made FAIR (published, traceable, accessible). Example: GA4GH Genomic Data Toolkit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reusability
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristics of data and their provenance should be described in detail according to domain-relevant community standards, with clear and accessible conditions for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide and publish accurate data descriptions, access and usage licenses, the community standards employed, and provenance for each dataset (example: BRCA Exchange).

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata and metadata standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata (broadly 'data about data') and metadata standards are central; they should be articulated and made publicly available to the greatest extent possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include systematic descriptions relevant to interpretation (bibliographic-like info) as well as data about theoretical assumptions, methods, provenance and context; formalise and continuously update community metadata standards to enhance reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-actionability
rubrics_metrics.description: Many aspects of data stewardship (indexation, retrieval, analysis) must be facilitated and executed by computers; FAIR should enable automation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design data, metadata and APIs to support automated retrieval and processing across levels of aggregation (from variant-level to aggregate catalogs); consider machine-actionability when specifying formats and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit, controlled access conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms and conditions under which data are shared or made accessible must be explicit, well-defined and readily available; FAIR supports controlled access models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document authentication/authorisation processes, publication/use embargos and structured access procedures. Promote the principle 'as open as possible, as closed as necessary' and clarify legitimate vs illegitimate means of controlling access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent metadata availability (even if data removed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata should remain accessible even when the underlying data are not available or no longer exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure repositories and indexes retain metadata; this supports discoverability and assessment of potential reuse without exposing sensitive data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique and persistent identifiers for datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets should be assigned unique and persistent identifiers to enable unequivocal identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use community-accepted persistent identifier systems to support referencing, indexing and long-term findability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and publication of standard technical and semantic formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Data and metadata should use common technical and semantic standards (formats, variables, ontologies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt domain-relevant standards; publish and make those standards traceable and accessible so that data consumers can interpret and integrate data reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalisation and publication of discipline-specific standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Community-specific data and metadata standards should be formalised and published to enable consistent stewardship and reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communities should coordinate to produce standards, maintain them, and provide metrics/incentives to stimulate adherence; successful platforms are often supported by closely-knit communities of practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisation, governance and coordination for data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective data sharing requires organisation and governance: collective oversight, reward mechanisms, coordination of research efforts and policy synchronisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop governance structures, coordinate policies across funders/journals/institutions, and create collective incentives and oversight to sustain sharing infrastructures and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair and impartial assessment of data access requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for access to controlled or sensitive datasets should be assessed in a fair and impartial manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish data access committees and transparent, unbiased review processes to adjudicate access, balancing privacy risks and research value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for design choices and provenance (vigilance about reuse limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research datasets embody design choices (sampling, measurement, categorisation) that must be made explicit and considered during reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document design choices and provenance in metadata; reusers must be vigilant and transparent about limitations; apply additional methodological checks, statistical innovations and active monitoring/correction of inadvertent biases to avoid misinterpretation and data-dredging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy by design and data protection measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Privacy and data protection should be built into data stewardship at every stage (privacy 'by design').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop frameworks and methods for privacy protection, implement structured consent protocols where appropriate, enforce rigorous access controls and accountability measures; consider GDPR implications such as data minimisation and rights around further processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant rights, governance and involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respecting participants' rights requires new governance frameworks and opportunities for participant involvement to foster trust and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include participant participation in governance, consider dynamic consent models and design governance to uphold trust, participation and appropriate control by data subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics oversight and accountability (ethics review boards and DACs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics review boards and data access committees are essential for assessing risks, benefits and appropriateness of data reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain ethics oversight and accountable review processes for sensitive human data; these bodies should be resourced and involved in access governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuing data sharing: metrics, incentives and credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop frameworks and metrics to justify investments in reuse and infrastructure and systems for credit that do not reproduce harmful reward systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create fair systems of scientific credit for data generation and reuse, fund sustainable infrastructures (possibly via overheads), and design incentives cautiously to avoid reinforcing 'publish or perish' pressures that harm research integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against harms from unqualified or incomplete FAIR application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying FAIR principles alone, without addressing normative and methodological challenges, can create additional issues (e.g., exacerbate bias or privacy harms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement FAIR with governance, privacy safeguards, methodological checks, and context-specific policies; coordinate policy-level instruments (mandates, management plans, codes of conduct) to ensure responsible implementation.
